proof_skeleton_nl: Use the divisibility inequalities only once, through the bottleneck realization lemma L1, to build a weighted complete intersection A whose Hilbert series is exactly the interval product in the theorem. By L2, the coefficient of q^j in that product is dim_Q A_j, hence is a nonnegative integer. Independently, L3 expands the same coefficient as the signed sum over X_j with sign (-1)^{|S|}. Lemma L4 rewrites that signed sum as E_j - O_j, where E_j and O_j count elements of X_j with even and odd subset parity respectively; therefore E_j >= O_j. Finally, L5 is a pure finite-set pairing lemma: whenever a finite set has at least as many 0-labeled elements as 1-labeled elements, one can pair every 1-labeled element with a distinct 0-labeled element and leave only 0-labeled fixed points. Applying it to X_j with label p(S,lambda)=|S| mod 2 produces the required involution iota_j. The theorem follows after unpacking the meaning of p.

steps.derives: There exists a family (f_s)_{s in I}, where I = {a+1,...,b}, of homogeneous polynomials in the weighted polynomial ring R := Q[x_s : s in I] with deg(x_s)=s and deg(f_s)=r+s, such that the ordered list by increasing s is a regular sequence.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the direct specialization of L1 to the parameters a, b, r from the theorem and the assumed inequalities M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for all positive integers d.

steps.derives: If A := R/(f_s : s in I), then [q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = dim_Q A_j, hence this coefficient is a nonnegative integer.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L2 to the regular sequence obtained in A1. L2 gives the Hilbert-series identity Hilb_A(q) = product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)). By definition of Hilb_A(q), the coefficient of q^j in this series is dim_Q A_j. Since dimensions of vector spaces are nonnegative integers, the coefficient is nonnegative.

steps.derives: [q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|}.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly L3 applied to the given integers a, b, r, j. The theorem's assumption 0 <= j <= floor(r(b-a)/2) implies in particular j >= 0, which is the only restriction needed in L3.

steps.derives: The set X_j is finite. If E_j is the number of elements (S,lambda) in X_j with |S| even and O_j is the number of elements (S,lambda) in X_j with |S| odd, then sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|} = E_j - O_j.
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct application of L4 to the same parameters a, b, r, j.
Both A3 and A4 compute the same signed sum over X_j, so substituting the expression from A4 into the equality from A3 gives the displayed identity.
A2 shows that the coefficient on the left side of A5 is nonnegative. A5 identifies that coefficient with E_j - O_j. Therefore E_j - O_j >= 0, i.e. E_j >= O_j.

steps.derives: There exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that whenever iota_j(x) != x, the parity label p(x) changes, and whenever iota_j(x) = x, one has p(x)=0, where p(S,lambda)=0 if |S| is even and p(S,lambda)=1 if |S| is odd.
steps.trivial_justification: Use L5 with X := X_j and with the label function p defined by the parity of |S|. Step A4 gives that X_j is finite. Step A6 gives that the number of p=0 elements is at least the number of p=1 elements, because those are exactly E_j and O_j. Therefore L5 yields an involution iota_j on X_j with the stated label-changing and fixed-point properties.

steps.derives: There exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.
steps.trivial_justification: In A7, p(S,lambda)=0 exactly means that |S| is even, and p(S,lambda)=1 exactly means that |S| is odd. Thus p(iota_j(S,lambda)) = 1 - p(S,lambda) is equivalent to |S'| being opposite in parity to |S|, i.e. |S'| ≡ |S| + 1 mod 2. The fixed-point condition p(S,lambda)=0 translates to |S| even. This is exactly the root theorem statement.
